https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2026-09-.text: Classic 105 Kiss 100 Homeboyz Radio Gukena FM East FM Radio Jambo X FM KWAYERA: Why Ruto stands to win State House race, despite contrary media Reasons: No credible opponents, just lightweights, tribalists and those with baggage while Ruto has made major development strides. Audio By Vocalize President William Ruto addresses residents of Buret in Kericho on September 10, 2026/PCS In spite of and despite everything written and said everywhere and anywhere, it still remains clear to me that President William Ruto will retain his seat as Kenya's CEO next year. Ruto is not the media's favourite contestant. Facts and data, however, back his return to office in August next year. There can be no denying the obvious fact that the most serious challenge Ruto faces is poor communication, not the o pposition. None other than Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale and former presidential a dviser Moses Kuria have publicly admitted to this blindingly obvious flaw. In articles published elsewhere, I have wondered three times since 2022 whether the Kenyan populace still trusts our mainstream media. I am still asking the same question today, even though our media is not the subject of my discussion here. From my personal lenses, both as a journalist and a Kenyan citizen, just as in 2022, I see Ruto winning the 2027 presidential contest without sweating so much, although that is not what I read, watch or listen to on a daily basis. The opposite is what flourishes. In the countdown to the 2022 general election, the entire Kenyan mainstream media and pollsters ganged up against the presidential candidacy of then Deputy President Ruto. The media rallied behind a s tate-backed contestant in the person of Raila Odinga of the Azimio l a Umoja c oalition headed by outgoing head of state Uhuru Kenyatta. As it turned out, the s tate project collapsed in our face and Ruto won the contest, albeit with a very slight margin. A similar situation a year earlier had manifested in Zambia where the entire Fourth Estate fraternity mobilised the populace to vote for incumben t Edgar Lungu to whom they gave a rating of more than 90 per cent, instead of Opposition leader Hakainde? Hichilema. Hungary witnessed the same trend early this year. Former Prime Minister Victor Orban’s Fidesz party lost in April to the pro-Western Tisza party although Orban was still reelected party leader. Since 2022, the media has refused to view Ruto from different binoculars. The President is still portrayed through the prisms of corruption, incompetence, disingenuity, dishonesty and other negative qualities. Although opinion polls still place Ruto slightly ahead as the pack leader in the battle for the House on the Hill after the August 10 , 2027 election, talk shows in broadcast media and mainstream print continually display him as the inevitable loser. I stick out my neck to predict a Ruto win next year. Not because Ruto is the most popular or cleverest politician town. But simply because he lacks a credible opponent to challenge him at the ballot. He has also done some tangible work to back his reelection bid. In the Equalisation Fund, universal healthcare, infrastructure, education, housing and sports, the Ruto regime has made remarkable strides and left unmistakable footprints, although bad publicity still mars the or reputation? of the Social Health Authority and affordable housing. The once highly heralded Hustler Fund seems to have fizzled out, it is neither here nor there. That notwithstanding, whichever way one looks at it, Ruto does not have a serious challenger at the moment. He is very unlikely to have one by next August, especially if we soberly cast our nets beyond ethnic barometers. What is more, those who have tossed their hats in the ring have so far not explained themselves to the electorate and laid out why they want to run for the presidency. Save for the collective sloganeering to remove Ruto from office , they have not presented any agenda that pushes the incumbent’s agenda and achievements to the back burner. In 2024, after Kalonzo Musyoka was invited to Raila's Bondo home as the guest of honour during the 80th birthday of Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga, I have more than once stated the former vice-president needed to start packaging himself as the most formidable o pposition leader and presidential candidate Kalonzo dilly-dallied. Raila died. Other figures have since cropped up to compete with him to be the anti-Ruto standard bearer. Kalonzo aside, today the o pposition has attracted impeached former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, former Justice Minister Martha Karua, former Attorney-General Justin Muturi, former Chief Justice David Kenani Maraga, rights activist Boniface Mwangi, former Defence Minister Eugene Wamalwa, businessman Jimi Wanjigi, lawyer George Wajackoya, gospel artiste Reuben Kigame and former Interior Cabinet Secretary Fred Matiang'i ¾ with Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna the newest kid on the block. For the longest time, Wanjigi has refused to transform himself into a top-tier presidential candidate. He remains a television and podcast aspirant. The former aide to former VP George Saitoti says all the right stuff about politics, governance and democracy. But it ends there. He has consistently failed to roll up his sleeves and join other opposition figures in the trenches, preferring instead to operate through a galaxy of proxies. That has allowed rookies to jump over him and start sharing meals with elders. Today, many people still don’t consider Wanjigi a serious contender. Former CJ Maraga is respected for being a stickler for constitutionalism. He earned world acclaim in September 2017 when his court overturned the election of President Uhuru Kenyatta, citing irregularities and illegalities, in a move that necessitated a repeat election a year later. But his achievements do not go beyond that. Since announcing his bid, Matiang'i has generally conducted himself reasonably well with much decorum and restraint, however, his past as Interior Minister leaves him in an abhorrent corner due to excesses by security forces . To his credit, Gachagua has sliced the entire populous Kikuyu vote from the Ruto political lump. However, the militant tribalistic anti-Ruto brickbats he hurls daily have only helped to rally a majority of the other communities behind Ruto. More than anyone else and any other reason, the DCP leader is the one person massively helping Ruto to gain support from other parts of the country outside of the former DP's Murima base. That cannot be good news for the o pposition at all. Karua, a former Justice Minister, is many things to many people. She will never erase the unfortunate events at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre in December 2007 when the victory of ODM presidential candidate Raila Odinga was stolen in favour of then-incumbent Mwai Kibaki. That paved the way for unprecedented genocide. Two years ago, it was widely reported in the media that President Ruto was constructing a state-of-the-art mega church at State House, using Sh1.2 billion of taxpayers’ money. The media has since gone silent on that subject. What happened? Last year, it was also widely reported that soldiers from the Somali autonomous federal state of Jubaland had invaded parts of North e astern where they had pitched tent and were calling the shots in the region, leading to closure of schools. That subject has also disappeared from the media. Again, what happened? Does anyone ask why Ruto likes addressing the public from the sunroofs of his cars? Aware of the media propaganda against him, he prefers to take his message directly to the electorate, I do believe. It will not surprise me when Ruto wins the next general election in r ound o ne. https://www.politico.eu/article/talking-.text: BRUSSELS — There is a growing realization among European governments that they may soon need to nominate someone to face Russian leader Vladimir Putin in direct talks on a peace deal for Ukraine. The main problem is deciding who should take on such a hazardous task. The question gained urgency this week after U.S. presidential envoy Steve Witkoff traveled to Russia to offer Putin a three-way summit with Donald Trump and Ukraine’s leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy, in an effort to press for a ceasefire. Advertisement Advertisement “President Putin disregards the European Union as an authority,” Czech President Petr Pavel said Tuesday in an interview with the Axel Springer Global Reporters’ Network, of which POLITICO is a part. “He doesn’t want to talk to Ursula von der Leyen, he doesn’t talk to Kaja Kallas. He stopped talking to other European leaders, including Emmanuel Macron.” He added that the EU should “identify a person or a group of people who would speak for Europe. Not necessarily representatives of the EU or NATO, but simply leaders who would be given a mandate by the others to negotiate.” Czech President Petr Pavel speaks during the 81st United Nations General Assembly at the United Nations Headquarters in New York, on September 23, 2026. | Timothy A. Clary/AFP via Getty Images In recent days, Trump has dismayed Ukraine and its European allies by talking over their heads with Putin and appearing increasingly willing to take Russia’s side in the almost five-year war. That has reignited debate in Brussels and beyond about the need for Europe to have its own direct line to the Kremlin to safeguard the region’s interests and bolster Ukraine’s ability to resist a lopsided deal. “Much as it sticks in the craw, I do think a channel of some kind to Putin would be a good thing to have,” said David Lidington, a distinguished fellow at the Royal United Services Institute in London. “I am not optimistic that it would achieve anything much in the short term, but to have a channel which can then be used as and when an opportunity arises is not a bad thing.” Diplomats and officials disagree on who would be the best person to represent Europe. Advertisement Advertisement Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, has negotiated directly with Trump on trade, while the president of the European Council, António Costa, has previously opened a line of communication with the Kremlin through his office. EU High Representative Kaja Kallas is another potential player who speaks for European interests as a whole. But the Brussels bubble needs to accept that a deal with Putin and Trump won’t be dictated by EU protocols, in the view of a diplomat from a European Union country who, like others in this article, was granted anonymity to discuss sensitive matters. “We cannot show up with two or three people all speaking on behalf of the EU,” the diplomat said. “The choice of who ends up representing the EU will be based on what would provide the most value, not personal power struggles or narcissistic preferences.” Will Stubb step up? One name outside the EU’s machinery that is gaining attention is Alexander Stubb, the president of Finland. Two key factors count in his favor: He has arguably the best relationship with Trump among EU leaders, and Finland has long experience of dealing with Russia — the two countries share a 1,300 kilometer border and have been at war in the past. Finland’s President Alexander Stubb delivers a joint press conference after a meeting on the situation in Ukraine on October 20, 2026 in Oslo. | Jonathan Nackstrand/AFP via Getty Images “Stubb is of interest because of Finnish knowledge of and traditional dialogue with Russia,” the diplomat said. “They know more than anyone on our side [about] what it takes to feel secure in such a situation.” A second EU diplomat noted that Stubb was “the only person who has come forward so far” to show high-level political leadership, and could serve as a European envoy at a future peace summit. Stubb was in Norway with Zelenskyy and Witkoff on Tuesday for negotiations ahead of the U.S. envoy’s visit to Russia to meet Putin. Advertisement Advertisement Also attending the gathering in Oslo was von der Leyen’s most senior aide, Bjoern Seibert, who has joined meetings of national security advisers as part of the Coalition of the Willing to support Ukraine. A third European diplomat said it was vital that the EU itself be represented in the talks, instead of a small grouping of powerful countries such as Germany, France and the U.K. That means both Seibert and Pedro Lourtie , the top aide to Costa, must have seats at the table during preparatory talks, the diplomat said, and that EU member countries must be properly updated on progress. Calling Costa According to a fourth EU diplomat, European leaders asked Costa at last week’s summit in Brussels whether it might be time for him to talk to Putin. “Costa said, no, he’s not going to talk to Putin now,” they said. “But Costa should start talking to Putin if we want to play a role in the negotiations. By not speaking, we are playing into the hands of our opponents.” The fourth diplomat said Costa would be a better choice than von der Leyen or Kallas, who are both seen as too invested in the Ukrainian side to represent the EU effectively at leader level. Kallas in particular has been outspoken in her criticism of Trump. “Costa comes across as more of an honest broker,” they summarized. The European Commission insists the EU is already present at the peace talks, flagging Seibert’s presence in Oslo on Tuesday. “The main aim [in Oslo] was to explore if the parameters are there for a possible move to trilateral or even multilateral talks with Ukraine and Russia present at the same table,” European Commission spokesperson Paula Pinho told reporters on Wednesday. She said the talks had focused on territory, security and post-war prosperity for Ukraine; Witkoff is expected to debrief Ukraine and the Europeans after his trip to meet Putin. “What is very important is that we are sitting at the table, that we are able to present our position, and that we can engage in what is a shared objective to put an end to this horrific war,” she added. Gerardo Fortuna and Paul Ronzheimer contributed to this report. Advertisement Advertisement
